To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The Featherweight Java (FJ) core calculus is expressive enough for a wide class of concurrent programs.

a reusable concurrency code generator should: • provide a portable assembly language that is easy to implement in a compiler and that is easy for an application programmer to use; • provide a set of concurrency primitives that are easy to use, but that are not too powerful; • provide a mechanism for implementing concurrency in a portable way; • provide a portable mechanism for implementing synchronization and memory management in a portable way.

a portable assembly language for a high-level language should include the following concurrency abstractions: a thread object that is a first-class object, a lightweight thread that is a second-class object, a thread-local variable, and a lock object that is a second class object.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a portable, reusable, and efficient code generator for concurrent programming languages.
how a language implementor can build an efficient, portable, and scalable implementation of a concurrent programming language.
the design of portable concurrency primitives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Featherweight Concurrency model is a good starting point for a portable concurrency model.
Featherweight Concurrent Java (FCJ) can be compiled into a portable assembly language that is a subset of the Java Virtual Machine.
we have a portable assembly language that can express concurrency and we have a code generator that generates code for this assembly language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a portable assembly language for concurrent programs.
the concurrency abstractions we have designed and implemented in the portable assembly language (PAL) are sufficient to compile the concurrent subset of the Java programming language.
we have designed and built a portable assembly-level language, Featherweight Concurrent C, and its compiler, Featherweight Concurrent GCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of concurrency is not as complicated as many believe.
it is feasible to implement a portable assembly language with a clean concurrency abstraction, and that this can be used as the basis of a portable concurrency library.
it is not necessary to have a special-purpose concurrency language to get good performance from a concurrent program.
